A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same zAImbardo study of guard–prisoner LLM interactions. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across the revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulations comprising 2,000 conversations across five LLMs, with human persuasion annotations, anti-social behavior measurements, and statistical analyses.

after.justification: V3 reports 2,400 conversations across six LLMs, retaining the original empirical analyses and adding persuasion re-annotation, detailed outcome breakdowns, and robustness analyses.

M1.justification: The toolkit architecture, shared/private prompt templates, role assignments, and conversation-generation procedure remain unchanged (v1 Appendices A–B; v3 Appendices B–C). Adding GPT-4.1 as an evaluated model and changing supplementary outcome scoring do not introduce a new simulation method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same prison environment, escape and additional-yard-time goals, five personality pairings, and risk/oversight conditions. V3's additional conversations extend model configurations within this coverage. Information-protection and policing scenarios are proposed future work, not evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: V3 adds GPT-4.1 to the evaluated roster of Llama3, Command-r, Orca2, Mixtral, and Mistral v0.2. The original five remain, and Mixtral and Mistral are still excluded from downstream behavioral analyses because of conversational failures, leaving four analyzed models instead of three.

E3.justification: V3 Appendix F.2 introduces an additional evaluation protocol that re-annotates previously successful conversations using clearer commitment requirements, excluding vague promises and unconfirmed supervisor referrals. The main permissive labels remain. The experimental total increases from 2,000 to 2,400 conversations, and the reported annotator panel increases from 13 to 15; the 19-message format and original decoding settings are retained.

E4.justification: V3 adds scenario-specific failure analyses (Tables 3–6), separates persuasion attempts from success conditional on attempting across personalities (Tables 8–12), and tests sensitivity to success definitions (Table 13). It also adds fractional-logit robustness checks for the bounded anti-social behavior outcomes, beyond v1's OLS analyses and existing temporal and Granger analyses.

E5.justification: V3 Table 7 adds Cohen's kappa for outcome and turn annotations, plus the mean and standard deviation of absolute turn disagreements, beyond v1 Table 3's disagreement counts. Fractional-logit checks add an alternative estimation procedure. Both versions already report ten repetitions per configuration, confidence intervals, standard deviations, and significance tests; no increase in repetitions is reported.

E6.justification: V3 adds GPT-4.1 outcomes and updates pooled estimates: the yard-time persuasion odds ratio changes from 9.31 to 35.07 after expanding the model pool, not as a same-setting performance gain. New Table 13 reports that stricter coding retains only 44 of 111 Llama3 yard-time successes and 4 of 118 GPT-4.1 successes. Detailed failure, conditional-success, and robustness results are also newly reported.

T1.justification: The OLS specification, Granger restricted model, F-statistic, and stationarity discussion are mathematically equivalent across versions. V3 adds empirical estimation and annotation checks, but no new mathematical definitions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The four research questions and central claims remain: goal difficulty principally affects persuasion, guard personas strongly influence anti-social behavior, undesirable behavior can emerge without negative persona prompts, and some models fail role adherence. The expanded model sample and supplementary checks do not replace these headline contributions.

C2.justification: V3 adds model safeguards as an alternative explanation for unattempted escapes, whereas v1 emphasizes anticipated difficulty. It explicitly limits its agents to role-playing LLMs without memory or environmental interaction, discusses the prison scenario's realism, and interprets stricter scoring as showing that persuasion is harder to establish. Most existing limitations and persona-based interpretations remain.

D1.justification: V3 Table 1 specifies the GPT-4.1 snapshot and context length, and the text identifies annotator affiliations and roles. The code reference changes to an anonymized repository described as providing code and generated conversations. V1's separate reproducibility statement, including installation, database, and analysis-script guidance, is removed; existing prompts and open-model hyperparameters remain documented.

R1.justification: V3 substantially expands positioning around multi-agent security, emergent misalignment, social conventions, and agent definitions, citing works such as Hammond et al. (2025), de Witt (2025), and Ashery et al. (2025). It sharpens the distinction between hierarchical interactions and interactions among equals, engages SPE criticism through Le Texier (2019), and removes some older general AI background references.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and substantial portions of the results and conclusions are rewritten. Conclusions move before limitations, the ethics statement becomes a broader-impact statement, the standalone reproducibility section disappears, and a new persuasion-results appendix reorganizes the supporting narrative.

P2.justification: V3 introduces ten additional tables and six fractional-logit figures, expands the annotation table with agreement statistics, and adds GPT-4.1 panels or series throughout existing displays. Figures and tables are extensively resized and relocated, and tighter line spacing changes the document layout beyond simple renumbering.

improvement.justification: V1 leaves the sensitivity of its permissive persuasion labels untested. V3 directly quantifies that important weakness: only 44 of 111 Llama3 yard-time successes survive stricter coding. Together with annotation-agreement statistics and fractional-logit checks, this substantially strengthens evidential transparency and robustness. The improvement is tempered by reporting inconsistencies, notably GPT-4.1 yard-time attempts disagreeing between Figure 2 and Table 8, and the removal of reproducibility setup guidance.
